key_fields.sql: select z.borough, count(*) as touches from lake.trips t join ops.zones z on z.locationid = t.pulocationid or z.locationid = t.dolocationid group by z.borough order by z.borough
key_fields.claim: An OR inside the JOIN condition cannot use a hash join; the engine falls back to a nested-loop style join, which is far more expensive than two equi-joins. (matched: inner join ops.zones z on z.locationid = t.pulocationid or z.locationid = t.dolocationid)

value.sql: SELECT z.Borough, COUNT(*) AS touches FROM (SELECT PULocationID AS LocationID FROM lake.trips UNION ALL SELECT DOLocationID FROM lake.trips) locs JOIN ops.zones z ON z.LocationID = locs.LocationID GROUP BY z.Borough ORDER BY z.Borough
value.change_summary: Replaced the OR join with UNION ALL of PULocationID and DOLocationID followed by a single equi-join to zones, enabling hash join optimization.
value.risk_notes: None; zones.LocationID is unique and the UNION ALL preserves exact duplicates from both columns, matching original semantics.
